settings.tagline: The GraphQL-first headless CMS in a single Rust binary
settings.description: Tess is a self-hostable, GraphQL-first headless CMS written in Rust. Define content models at runtime, publish with review workflows, and run it on Docker, a VM or AWS Lambda.
settings.footerText: © 2026 Tess Dev Team. Community edition for personal use, Enterprise edition for commercial use.

data.title: Tess vs Contentful
data.description: Tess compared with Contentful (Composable content platform (SaaS)): An enterprise headless CMS delivered as SaaS, with REST and GraphQL delivery APIs and a large app ecosystem.

competitor.name: Contentful
competitor.summary: An enterprise headless CMS delivered as SaaS, with REST and GraphQL delivery APIs and a large app ecosystem.

rows.other: REST delivery and management APIs, plus a GraphQL Content API

rows.tess: Admin UI or API, applied immediately
rows.other: Web app or management API, with environments

rows.tess: Community free for personal use; Enterprise license for commercial use
rows.other: Free tier, then paid plans with usage limits

competitor.chooseThem: - You need an enterprise SaaS with SLAs, many locales and a large app marketplace.
competitor.chooseTess:
- You want to own the infrastructure and the data.
- You prefer a predictable license to usage-based limits.
competitor.migration: Contentful content types and their fields map to Tess content types; references become `RELATION` fields and assets become `Asset` relations. Import the models with `tess-transfer`, then copy entries with the Contentful export and the Tess GraphQL API.
